messages:
incident-bot: AUTO-PAGER triggered for service redwood-infer-prod at 2026-03-15T03:12:09Z. Alert: p99 latency 2.5s (SLO 1.2s), streaming stalls detected on model-x-int8-v2. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/alerts/5723456789. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/streaming-latency. Please ACK and start triage.
emma-oncall: ack — I'm oncall. Starting triage, joining now.
jason-runtime: looking at runtime logs. I see a calibration rollout job for int8-profile v2 at 03:12:02 that triggered a profile_update and subsequent kv-cache flush across riders. Correlated spike right after.
liam-platform: metrics: p95 rose from ~420ms -> ~900ms, p99 to 2.5s. Error rate small bump ~0.2%. KV cache hit-rate dropped from 92% -> 61% after the rollout. Region: eu-west-1 and us-west-2 most affected.
maya-support: CS: customer AtlasAI opened a high-sev ticket reporting streaming stalls and long tail responses in production. They're seeing sessions hang then resume.
jason-runtime: that matches. The calib job is doing a global flush of in-memory quant caches. For long-context streaming, KV misses are expensive — we hit dequant/kern stalls.
emma-oncall: can we fallback traffic to the fp16 variant for model-x while we triage? Need quick mitigation.
jason-runtime: yes — we have model-x-fp16. I can update routing policy to prefer it. Will do staged shift: 10% -> 100% if metrics look good.
deploy-bot: route-change initiated: model-x routing preference set to model-x-fp16 10% canary in eu-west-1. Job id: rc-5723.
emma-oncall: monitoring p99 and streaming stall count.
liam-platform: after 10% shift p99 still 1.9s (down from 2.5s). Proceed?
emma-oncall: bump to 50%.
deploy-bot: route-change progress: 50% -> applied.
liam-platform: p99 now 1.3s. Streaming stalls count decreased by 65%.
emma-oncall: increase to 100% fallback.
deploy-bot: route-change progress: 100% -> applied.
liam-platform: post-100% shift p99 1.05s, p95 340ms. Streaming stall alerts clearing. Note: cost per request up ~18% on fallback path.
jason-runtime: still seeing a small tail cluster for long-context (>8k tokens) traces — kv-miss rate still elevated in a few riders. I think the calibration flush cleared warm KV entries and some background workers haven't rehydrated yet.
naomi-ml: confirmed: the calibration job currently forces a global profile swap that invalidates cached quant kernels and associated kv cache entries. We didn't have a warmup phase in the rollout.
emma-oncall: start runbook mitigation step: warm caches.
runbook-bot: replay-warm job enqueued. Spinning up background replay of prefix-heavy traces at 2% background QPS against model-x-int8-v2 in a canary group. Job id: warm-5723.
liam-platform: warm job reports initial 1000 traces processed, KV hit-rate climbing back to 80% in canary riders.
maya-support: AtlasAI reports improvement — they say sessions recovered, occasional slow responses only. CS drafting customer update.
emma-oncall: summarizing root cause for SE/CS: int8 calibration rollout triggered global kv-cache flush + kernel/quant variant swap. That produced transient KV miss storms and kernel contention on long streaming contexts, causing p99 breach and streaming stalls. Mitigation taken: immediate routing fallback to fp16 variant + cache warming job. Current status: mitigated, routing fallbacks at 100%.
alex-product: any user-facing errors or data loss? Need notes for post-incident comms.
maya-support: no request failures recorded, just high latency and stalls; sessions resumed. AtlasAI has been notified and is satisfied with mitigation for now.
jason-runtime: action items: 1) revert global cache flush behavior in calibration; 2) implement staged rollout with warmup step and canary gating; 3) add KV prefill step to calibration pipeline. I'll open PRs for the runtime changes.
naomi-ml: action items on ML side: add flag no_global_kv_flush and implement incremental kernel swap that warms quant kernels on a subset before global switch. Also add telemetry for kernel swap durations. I'll own the ML PR.
liam-platform: platform follow-ups: add alert for sudden KV hit-rate drop correlated with calib jobs and a safeguard to block global rollouts if hit-rate delta > 20%.
emma-oncall: assigning follow-ups: jason-runtime (runtime changes), naomi-ml (calib workflow), liam-platform (alerting), maya-support (customer comms). ETA 2-4 hours for change plans, longer for rollout.
emma-oncall: closing pager — status set to mitigated. Will hand off to regular oncall follow-up channel for postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident status updated to MITIGATED by emma-oncall at 2026-03-15T03:26:30Z. Pager cleared.
emma-oncall: any objections to marking this resolved and scheduling a postmortem doc? No? I'll file postmortem and link.
runbook-bot: Postmortem template created: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/5723456789-postmortem.
emma-oncall: thanks all — great triage.
